en.name: Macadamias, shelled
en.summary: Shelled macadamias keep only 2–4 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, but 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). That enormous gap is the whole story: macadamias are the fattiest nut on the shelf, and cold is what protects the fat.
en.pantry: 2–4 weeks from purchase in a cool, dark cupboard, in an airtight jar. That is a short window for something that looks so durable, and it surprises people — but a macadamia is roughly three-quarters oil, and once the shell is off, that oil is exposed to air. Nothing is growing in the jar; the nut is simply oxidising, and warmth and light speed it up. A bag bought loose from a bulk bin may already be part way through this, so buy from somewhere with turnover.
en.fridge: 12 months from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, sealed. Refrigerating nuts feels like fussy advice until you see the numbers: the cupboard gives you weeks and the fridge gives you a year, because cold slows oxidation down by roughly an order of magnitude. Use a genuinely airtight jar — macadamias are bland and fatty, which makes them excellent at absorbing the smell of everything else in the fridge.
en.freezer: 24 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), which is the sensible home for anything more than a week's worth. Bag them airtight with the air pressed out, or double-bag. There is very little water in a macadamia, so freezing does not damage the texture at all and they can be chopped or eaten straight from frozen once they have taken the chill off.
en.thawing: No real thawing needed. Let the sealed bag come back to room temperature before opening it so condensation does not settle on the nuts and make them soft.
spoilage: A bitter, sharp or paint-like taste — rancid oil, and one nut will tell you.
A smell like old cooking oil or crayons rather than sweet and buttery.
A soft, chewy nut instead of a crisp one, meaning it has taken up moisture.
Mould or a musty smell, which only happens in a damp container.
tips: Buy small quantities from a shop with turnover; shelled macadamias are already on the clock.
Freeze the bulk and keep a small jar in the fridge for daily use.
Taste one before baking with them — rancidity carries straight into the cookie.
Keep them sealed in the fridge and freezer; they soak up other foods' smells.

faq.q: How long do macadamia nuts keep?
faq.a: 2–4 weeks from purchase in the cupboard, 12 months in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 24 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Should macadamias be kept in the fridge?
faq.a: Yes, if you are not going to eat them within a few weeks. They are the fattiest common nut, and the fridge takes them from weeks to a year.

faq.q: How can you tell if macadamias have gone bad?
faq.a: Eat one. Rancid macadamia is sharply bitter and tastes like old oil. Softness on its own is moisture rather than spoilage.

zh.name: 夏威夷豆（去殼）
zh.summary: 去殼夏威夷豆放櫥櫃，自購買日起只有 2～4 週；但 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍可放 24 個月。這個誇張的落差就是重點：夏威夷豆是架上油脂最高的堅果，而保護油脂的正是低溫。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼避光的櫥櫃，自購買日起 2～4 週。對一個看起來這麼耐放的東西來說，這個窗口短得讓人意外——但夏威夷豆大約四分之三是油，去殼之後那些油就直接暴露在空氣裡。罐子裡沒有東西在生長，堅果只是在氧化，而溫度和光線會讓它加速。散裝秤來的可能已經走了一段路，所以請找流通量大的店家買。
zh.fridge: 密封放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 12 個月。把堅果冰起來聽起來很龜毛，看到數字就不會這麼想了：櫥櫃給你幾週，冰箱給你一年，因為低溫把氧化速度拉慢了一個數量級。請用真正氣密的罐子——夏威夷豆味道淡、油脂多，吸別人味道的能力一流。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 24 個月；只要超過一週的量，冷凍就是合理的歸宿。請把空氣壓出來密封，或雙層裝袋。夏威夷豆含水極少，冷凍完全不傷質地，稍微退冰後就能直接切碎或直接吃。
zh.thawing: 談不上解凍。請讓密封袋回到室溫再打開，免得水氣凝在堅果上讓它變軟。
spoilage: 嚐起來發苦、尖銳或有油漆味——那是油耗，吃一顆就知道。
聞起來像久放的食用油或蠟筆，而不是奶香甜香。
咬起來是軟韌的而不是脆的，代表吸了水氣。
容器潮濕才會出現的霉點或霉味。
tips: 跟流通快的店家買小份量；去殼的夏威夷豆本來就在倒數。
大包冷凍，冷藏留一小罐當日常取用。
拿去烘焙前先吃一顆，油耗味會原封不動進到餅乾裡。
冷藏冷凍都要密封，它很會吸別的食物的味道。

faq.a: 自購買日起，放櫥櫃 2～4 週，4 °C 以下冷藏 12 個月，−18 °C 冷凍 24 個月。
如果幾週內吃不完，要。它是常見堅果裡油脂最高的，冷藏能把「幾週」變成「一年」。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷夏威夷豆壞了？
faq.a: 吃一顆。油耗的夏威夷豆苦得很尖銳，像放久的油。單純變軟只是受潮，不是腐敗。
